title: A short history of the bicycle
text:
The bicycle is one of the simplest and most successful machines ever invented. Its ancestor appeared in Germany in 1817, when Karl von Drais built a wooden 'running machine' {A}. It had no pedals, and riders had to push themselves along with their feet.

Pedals came about forty years later, when French mechanics attached them directly to the front wheel {B}. These early bicycles were nicknamed 'boneshakers', since the iron wheels made every stone on the road painfully obvious. The next version, the 'penny-farthing', had an enormous front wheel, {C}, but it was dangerous: a rider who hit an obstacle could be thrown over the handlebars.

The breakthrough came in the 1880s with the 'safety bicycle', which had two wheels of equal size and a chain driving the back wheel. Rubber tyres filled with air soon made riding comfortable, {D}. Suddenly everybody wanted one, including women, for whom the bicycle became a symbol of independence.

Today more than a billion bicycles are in use around the world. Cities such as Copenhagen and Amsterdam have built hundreds of kilometres of cycle lanes, {E}, and electric models allow people to travel further without getting tired. Perhaps the secret of the bicycle's success is that its design has hardly changed, {F}.
